To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the disassembly of a PixD-PixEsensor complex takes place only after the photoactivation of two subunits in the dark complex.
the interprotein reaction of PixD and PixE is light-intensity-dependent.
the disassembly reaction of PixD(10) and PixE(5) complexes is light-intensity-dependent, and two PixD sub-units in the complex need to be photoactivated to dissociate the complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of light signal transduction by the PixD-Pix complex, and we have succeeded in clarifying the light-intensity dependence in this system.
elucidating the molecular mechanisms of interprotein signal transfer and provides a novel insight into the biological response of the PixD-PixEs complex.
the dynamics of the light signal transduction process in a biological system, and we have succeeded in tracking the reaction of a protein complex in real time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PixD-PixD interaction is essential to initiate signal transduction.
the light intensity-dependent signal transduction in the PixD-PixD-PixE photoreceptor complex is initiated by a light-intensity-dependent disassembly of the complex.
PixD-PixD dimerization is essential for the light-dependent signal transduction of PixE, which is the first report for a BLUF-type protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PixD-PixD interaction is essential for the biological function of PixD.
the PixD-Pix complex acts as a sensor of the light intensity, and the light signal transduction is initiated only after the activation of the complex.
the PixD-PixD-PixE(5) complex acts as a light sensor with a threshold of 0.1 μmol m-2s-1, and this threshold is determined by the requirement of two photons for the dissociation of the complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the light intensity-dependent response is a common feature of light signaling in the BLUF family.
the PixD(5)-PixE(3) light complex dissociates only when two PixD subunit molecules are photoactivated.
the PixD-PixD interaction is essential for light intensity detection, which may be a common mechanism for BLUF proteins.
